translation: The Blessed Lord said: I taught this eternal science of Yoga to Vivasvan (the sun-god or ancient king); Vivasvan taught it to Manu; and Manu communicated it to Ikshvaku.
simple_explanation: In a prior birth, the soul of Krishna existed as a sage (such as Vashistha) who instructed the ruler Vivasvan. These names also reflect titles of functional competence based on Vedic political science.

translation: Handed down thus in continuous succession, the royal sages (Rajarshiyah) knew this science. But by the great lapse of time, O scorcher of foes, this Yoga was lost to the world.
That very ancient Yoga is being declared to you by Me today, because you are My devotee and dear friend; it is indeed a profound secret (uttamam rahasyam).
Arjuna said: Your birth is recent, whereas the birth of Vivasvan happened in ancient times. How am I to understand that You taught this science in the beginning?
The Blessed Lord said: Many births of Mine and yours have passed, O Arjuna. I remember all of them, but you do not remember them, O terror of foes.

Though I am unborn, imperishable by nature, and the Lord of all created beings, yet, governing My own material nature, I manifest myself through My own creative power (atma- mayaya), driven by a pure desire for public welfare.
simple_explanation: According to Yoga Sutras, nature serves two purposes: experience (bhoga) and liberation (apavarga). When a purified soul attains liberation, his latent, selfless urge to help others prompts him to request the Divine for an opportunity to take a physical form to guide humanity. This is a deliberate incarnation (Atmamaya), not a standard birth driven by binding karma.

translation: Whenever there is a decline in righteousness (Dharma) and a rise in lawlessness, O Bharata, then I manifest Myself, obtaining birth from the Supreme Lord for public welfare.
simple_explanation: These words are spoken by Krishna as a highly evolved, spiritually empowered soul (Yogashakti-sampanna jivatma), not as the abstract Omnipresent God, for later in 18.61, he explicitly directs Arjuna to seek shelter in the Lord who dwells within the hearts of all.

translation: For the protection of the righteous, for the destruction of wicked evildoers, and for firmly re- establishing righteousness, I manifest myself age after age.

He who understands the divine nature of My manifestation and actions in their true essence, does not take an ordinary, reward-driven birth upon leaving the body; he joins the ranks of divine workers, O Arjuna.
Freed from attachment, fear, and anger, completely absorbed in Me, and taking refuge in Me, many purified by the austerity of wisdom (Jnana-tapasa) have attained My state of being.
In whatever way people approach Me and offer their services to this mission, I reward and utilize them accordingly. Human beings follow My path in every way, O Partha.
Those who long for success in their actions worship worldly cosmic powers here; for in the human world, success born of action is achieved quickly.

The fourfold social order (Chaturvarnya) was created by Me according to the classification of human aptitude and corresponding actions (Guna-karma-vibhagashah). Though I am its secondary historical restorer, know Me to be non-attached and immutable.
simple_explanation: In this era, people have reduced social classification to a mere hereditary birthright. I restored the authentic system based on natural attributes and conduct. For this reason, I chose to dine at the house of Vidura, who was considered low-born, rather than at Duryodhana's palace. Shishupala insulted me by calling me a mere cowherd, but I recognize merit, not birth. The ultimate author of this system is God via the Veda.

translation: Actions do not taint Me, nor do I have any longing for the rewards of actions. He who understands Me as such is never bound by the chain of actions.
Knowing this, ancient seekers of liberation performed actions in early times. Therefore, you should perform your designated Kshatriya duty, just as it was performed by the ancestors in earlier ages.

What is right action (Karma) and what is inaction (Akarma)? Even the wise are confused in this regard. I shall explain that action to you, knowing which you will be freed from this inappropriate delusion.

One must understand the nature of right action (Karma), understand the nature of prohibited or wrong action (Vikarma), and also understand the nature of non-action (Akarma). The track of action is profound and complex.
He who perceives inaction in right action, and right action in inaction, is wise among human beings; he is integrated (Yuktah) and a performer of total action.
simple_explanation: Every good action can turn into a bad action depending on the context. If a sentry guarding a critical fortress abandons his post because it is time for his evening prayers, his conventional prayer becomes a highly sinful act of omission. Conversely, if an enemy uses a herd of cows as a shield to destroy a nation, shooting through the herd to neutralize the enemy transforms an apparently bad act (killing cows) into a mandatory act of public preservation. One who sees this boundary is wise.

translation: He whose undertakings are all free from personal longing and selfish motive, and whose actions are burnt up by the fire of true knowledge, is called a learned person (Pandita) by the wise.

Having renounced all attachment to the fruits of action, ever content, and dependent on nothing, he does not perform any binding action even while remaining fully engaged in undertakings. He is like an executioner carrying out a legal sentence—free from personal malice.
Exempt from expectations, with his mind and self controlled, and having discarded all possessiveness, he incurs no sin while performing bare physical actions for bodily sustenance.
Content with whatever comes unsolicited, rising above dualities, free from envy, and remaining even-minded in both success and failure, he is not bound even though he performs actions.

The actions of a person who is free from attachment, liberated, whose mind is anchored in wisdom, and who acts solely for the sake of sacrifice (Yajna), are completely dissolved without binding outcomes.

The offering is Brahman; the oblation is Brahman; it is poured by Brahman into the fire of Brahman. Brahman alone shall be attained by him who is fully absorbed in actions dedicated to Brahman (Brahma-karma-samadhina).
simple_explanation: Every specific action must be executed with the Divine as its final goal. The life energy and resources given to us belong to the Lord. Offering them back to look after His creation is true Havi (oblation). A liberated worker finds a transcendental joy even in the hardships of public service.

translation: Some Yogis perform sacrifices dedicated to the cosmic powers (Daiva Yajna), learning light and stability from natural elements or modeling their behavior on noble minds. Others offer sacrifice into the fire of Brahman through the performance of ritual duties.
Some offer their hearing and other senses into the fires of self-restraint (Sanyama-agnishu). Others offer sound and other sense objects into the fires of the senses (Indriya-agnishu).
simple_explanation: Offering sense objects into the fires of the senses means interacting with the world scientifically and detachedly. For instance, a medical scientist examines a diseased, explicit part of a human body with deep accuracy. He remains completely free from lust, focused purely on finding a cure. This is a scientific sacrifice for public good.

translation: Others offer all the activities of their senses and vital life currents (Prana-karmani) into the fire of the Yoga of self-restraint, which is illuminated by true knowledge.

Some perform sacrifice through material wealth (Dravya-yajna), some through austerity (Tapo-yajna), some through the practice of Yoga, and others, who are ascetics of rigid vows, perform sacrifice through scriptural study and knowledge.

Others offer the incoming vital breath (Prana) into the outgoing breath (Apana), and the outgoing breath into the incoming breath. Restraining the pathways of both breaths, they remain absorbed in breath control (Pranayama).

Others, regulating their diet (niyata-aharah), offer their vital energies into their respective vital functions. All these are knowers of sacrifice (Yajnavidah), and their sins are destroyed through these sacrifices.

Those who consume the immortal nectar of the remnants of sacrifice (Yajna-shishta-amrita) attain the eternal Brahman. Even this world is not for the non-sacrificing person; how then can the next world be his, O best of the Kurus?
simple_explanation: This verse strikes down medieval superstition regarding an "invisible merit" (Adrishta) separated from rational outcome. Medieval ritualists claimed that executing absurd rituals produced a magical, invisible benefit in the afterlife. The Gita emphasizes that a sacrifice must first improve this life; if it cannot make this world orderly and happy, it cannot fix the afterlife.

translation: Thus, many forms of sacrifice are spread out in the pages of the Veda. Know all of them to be born of right action; knowing this, you shall be completely liberated. Do not stay inactive.
The sacrifice of knowledge (Jnana-yajna) is superior to any material sacrifice, O scorcher of foes! All actions in their entirety culminate in realized wisdom (Jnane parisamapyate), O Partha.

Learn that true knowledge by prostrating yourself before wise mentors, by questioning them with a clean spirit, and by serving them. Sages who have realized the essential Truth will instruct you in that wisdom.
Knowing that truth, O Pandava, you will never fall into such delusion again. By this wisdom, you will see all living beings within your own expanded vision, and thus within My global mission.
Even if you were the most sinful of all sinners, you will cross over the ocean of all misdeeds by boarding the boat of this selfless cosmic wisdom.
Just as a blazing fire reduces fuel to ashes, O Arjuna, the fire of this selfless knowledge reduces all binding outcomes of actions to ashes. It cuts the root of selfishness.

There is no purifier in this world equal to the knowledge of sacrificing the individual for the collective good. He who becomes perfected in Yoga automatically discovers this truth within himself over time.
A person endowed with faith (Shraddhavan), who is fully dedicated to it, and who has mastered his senses, obtains this wisdom. Having obtained it, he swiftly attains supreme peace (Param shantim).
An ignorant person, devoid of faith, and possessed of a doubting mind (samshay-atma), goes to ruin. For the doubting soul, there is neither happiness in this world nor in the next.
Actions do not bind him who has dedicated his actions to God through Yoga, whose doubts are slashed by realized wisdom, and who is poised in self-possession, O Dhananjaya.

Therefore, slash with the sword of wisdom this doubt lingering in your heart, which has arisen out of a temporary clouding by family attachment. Establish yourself firmly in Yoga and arise, O Bharata!
